requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark as described in UN R10 paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every rear lamp ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
The international approval mark affixed to the rear lamp ESA shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.

The international approval mark affixed to the rear lamp ESA shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle containing the letter "E".
The rear lamp ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for conducted emissions.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband emission limit for the rear lamp ESA in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband emission limit for the rear lamp ESA in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband emission limit for the rear lamp ESA in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
The broadband emission values measured on the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the ESA broadband type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
Where measured using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured narrowband emission value of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The transient conducted disturbance emission of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the positive transient conducted pulse amplitude emitted by the rear lamp ESA shall not exceed +75 V.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the negative transient conducted pulse amplitude emitted by the rear lamp ESA shall not exceed -100 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the positive transient conducted pulse amplitude emitted by the rear lamp ESA shall not exceed +150 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the negative transient conducted pulse amplitude emitted by the rear lamp ESA shall not exceed -450 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
For the stripline method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
For the TEM cell method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
For the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
For the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
For the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the stripline method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
For the TEM cell method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
For the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
For the ALSE method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
For the reverberation chamber method, the rear lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
The rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the rear lamp ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for starting profile according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the rear lamp ESA for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

Where the rear lamp ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, it shall withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, meeting functional status B for immunity related functions where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, C for immunity related functions of other ESA, and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems for 500 pulses with FPSC III for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems for 500 pulses with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems for 10 pulses with FPSC II for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a at -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Where the rear lamp ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.

Where the rear lamp ESA is not switched, contains no switches or does not include inductive load, it need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the vehicle immunity test field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, the vehicle immunity test field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 with the ISO 11451-4 BCI method, the vehicle immunity test current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" of the vehicle representative of its type, according to paragraph 2.2. of Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall be 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband emission limit for the rear lamp ESA shall remain constant at 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The broadband emission values measured on the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The dimension a of the UN Regulation No. 10 approval mark affixed to the ESA shall be at least 6 mm.
The broadband electromagnetic emissions test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emissions test.
Where the broadband emissions test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA should be tested at rated current.
For an ESA not involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emissions test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.

The broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for narrowband electromagnetic emissions according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 8.
The rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband electromagnetic emission tests.

The narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp electrical/electronic sub-assembly shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the results cover the full frequency range of 20 to 6,000 MHz.
The ESA shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with AM (amplitude modulation) test signals of 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) test signals of Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) test signals of Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA shall meet the radiated immunity requirements when tested in an absorber chamber according to ISO 11452-2, using the substitution method to establish the test field conditions.
The ESA shall meet the absorber chamber immunity requirements when tested with vertical polarization.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements when tested in a TEM cell according to ISO 11452-3.

The ESA shall meet the bulk current injection immunity requirements when tested according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench using either the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA or the BCI closed loop method with the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.

Where the ESA is tested while installed in the vehicle as an alternative, the ESA shall meet the bulk current injection immunity requirements when tested according to ISO 11451-4 using the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements when tested by stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements when tested in a reverberation chamber according to ISO 11452-11, using a test setup with ground plane unless otherwise specified.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ESA shall be immune to test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, unless the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the rear lamp ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be determined according to ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

Each lamp forming part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear lamp unit (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall satisfy the provisions of UN Regulation No. 148 or of another applicable Regulation.
A lamp not satisfying the provisions of UN Regulation No. 148 or of any other applicable Regulation shall not be part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear lamp unit.
The rear position lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol R1.
The rear position lamp (variable) shall be identified by the symbol R2.
The stop lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol S1.
The stop lamp (variable) shall be identified by the symbol S2.
The reversing lamp shall be identified by the symbol AR, where the letters A and R may be mingled.
Every rear lamp belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value for "a" in the size of the approval marking on the rear lamp shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking on the rear lamp shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking on the rear lamp shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number in the approval marking on the rear lamp shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking on the rear lamp shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.

The approval marking on the rear lamp shall include the number of UN Regulation No. 148 followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Where the rear lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the rear lamp shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
The horizontal mounting arrow on a rear position lamp that cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The horizontal mounting arrow on a reversing lamp shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
The rear lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The rear lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage in the case of a lamp with an electronic light source control gear.
The rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage in the case of a lamp with a variable luminous intensity control.
The rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage in the case of a lamp with a secondary operating mode.
The rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage in the case of a lamp with non-replaceable light sources.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used in the rear lamp, each light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used in the rear lamp, each light source module shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
The specific identification code of a replaceable light source module shall comprise the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle.
Where several non-identical replaceable light source modules are used in the rear lamp, the specific identification code of each module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
The approval mark on a replaceable light source module and the approval mark on the rear lamp in which the module is used shall both be from the same applicant.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used in the rear lamp, each light source module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the rear lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the rear lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.

The approval marking of the rear lamp shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
The approval marking of the lamp shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.

The category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
Where an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps complying with several UN Regulations, the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall have been found to comply with the requirements of each of those UN Regulations.
Where a single approval mark is affixed on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the approval mark shall be visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps bear a single approval mark, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN Regulation No. 148.

The lamp shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.

Where a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp using a common light source and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

In a rear lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a rear lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.

Where compliance in case of single light source failure is achieved by meeting the minimum intensity, the maximum intensities of the rear lamp shall not be exceeded when all light sources are illuminated.
Where compliance in case of single light source failure is achieved by a tell-tale signal, the rear lamp shall be only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

The rear lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
The rear lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
Where the rear lamp has replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
Where the rear lamp has replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
Where the rear lamp has replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.
Where the rear lamp has replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tool(s), not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.

Where the rear lamp has replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tool(s), not be interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

Where the rear lamp has replaceable light source module(s), the photometric requirements of the device shall be met when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code.

Where the rear lamp is equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the rear lamp shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
Unless otherwise specified, the luminous intensities of the rear lamp functions shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.

Where measurement results are challenged, the luminous intensity requirement of the rear lamp for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the rear lamp for testing shall be 6.75 V for 6 Volt-Systems.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the rear lamp for testing shall be 13.5 V for 12 Volt-Systems.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the rear lamp for testing shall be 28 V for 24 Volt-Systems.

Where the rear lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and uses light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.
The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The luminous intensity of the lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.

Where a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone shall be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.

Where one or both of the reciprocally incorporated rear position lamp and stop lamp contain more than one light source and are considered as a single lamp, the luminous intensity ratio of at least 5:1 shall be met with all sources in operation.
The luminous intensities of the lamp shall comply when tested according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall meet the colorimetric characteristics inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall be observed.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of rear position lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.

For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of up to 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The minimum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) on the reference axis shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) when used as a single lamp shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) marked "D" shall be 8.5∙10^0 cd.
The standard light distribution of a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) shall comply with Figure A3-I.
The minimum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 5∙10^-2 cd.
The minimum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) on the reference axis shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) when used as a single lamp shall be 4.2∙10^1 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) marked "D" shall be 2.1∙10^1 cd.
The standard light distribution of a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) shall comply with Figure A3-I.
The minimum luminous intensity of a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 5∙10^-2 cd.
The minimum luminous intensity of the rear position lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as specified in Table 4.
The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity when used as a single lamp shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd.
For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity for a lamp marked "D" shall be 1.30∙10^2 cd.
For a stop lamp of category S1, the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
For a stop lamp of category S1, the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 3∙10^-1 cd.
For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the maximum luminous intensity when used as a single lamp shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd.
For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the maximum luminous intensity for a lamp marked "D" shall be 3.65∙10^2 cd.

For a stop lamp of category MS (steady), the maximum luminous intensity for a lamp marked "D" shall be 1.30∙10^2 cd.
For a stop lamp of category MS, the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
For a stop lamp of category MS, the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 3∙10^-1 cd.

The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (category AR) below 5°D shall be 8.00∙10^3 cd.
The standard light distribution of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall be as defined in Figure A3-V.
The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
For production lamps, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.

For a required minimum value of 3∙10^-1 cd, the measured value of a production lamp shall be at least 2∙10^-1 cd (20 per cent equivalent) or 1∙10^-1 cd (30 per cent equivalent).
For a required minimum value of 7∙10^-2 cd, the measured value of a production lamp shall be at least 5∙10^-2 cd (20 per cent equivalent) or 3∙10^-2 cd (30 per cent equivalent).
For a required minimum value of 5∙10^-2 cd, the measured value of a production lamp shall be at least 3∙10^-2 cd (20 per cent equivalent) or 2∙10^-2 cd (30 per cent equivalent).

The light intensity of the rear position lamp, in the various directions of measurement, shall not be less than the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

The photometric intensity of the rear position lamp, where the lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, shall be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

The photometric intensity of the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS, where the lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, shall be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

The light intensity of the rear position lamp in each direction of a part of the light distribution field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

The light intensity of the stop lamp in each direction of a part of the light distribution field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

The reversing lamp, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, shall have no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.

The rear position lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, giving for the various directions of measurement the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in the relevant tables.

The stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, giving for the various directions of measurement the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in the relevant tables.
The rear position lamp and the stop lamp shall comply with the standard light distribution shown in Figure A3-I.

The reversing lamp shall emit, for the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference (H = 0°, V = 0°), at least the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.

The chromaticity coordinates of each light function of the rear lamp shall comply with the required values when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148.
For the reversing lamp using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For the reversing lamp using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For the rear position lamp using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For the rear position lamp using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For the stop lamp using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For the stop lamp using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
The luminous intensity distribution of each light function of the rear lamp shall, depending on the light source technology, additionally comply at the point in time listed in Table A8-1.
The rear position lamp function shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements at point HV at 4 seconds after switch ON, where additional testing at points in time is required.
The stop lamp function shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements at point HV at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, where additional testing at points in time is required.
The reversing lamp function shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements at point HV at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, where additional testing at points in time is required.
