The approval number assigned to the retro-reflector type shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.
The approval marking of a retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent) shall bear the symbol IA with a minimum value of "a" of 5 mm.
The approval marking of a retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight shall bear the symbol IB with a minimum value of "a" of 5 mm.
The change index for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent) shall be 0 for the 00 series of amendments and 1 for the 01 series of amendments.
The change index for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight shall be 0 for the 00 series of amendments and 1 for the 01 series of amendments.

Every retro-reflecting device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the retro-reflecting device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The size of the approval marking on the retro-reflecting device shall comply with the value for "a" defined in Table 1.

The approval marking of the retro-reflector shall include the approval mark, consisting of a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking of the retro-reflector shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark on the retro-reflector.
The approval marking of the retro-reflector shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.

The approval marking of the retro-reflector shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Where the approval marking of the retro-reflector is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in the Regulation.
The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings required in paragraph 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps of the rear lamp, the single approval mark shall be visible after installation of the lamps.

Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps of the rear lamp, no light-transmitting part of the lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.

The size of the components of a single approval mark on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The retro-reflector shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in those sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval.

The retro-reflector shall meet the requirements pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which it is intended to be installed, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough.
Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.

Where the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The retro-reflecting optical units and filters of the retro-reflector shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflector, when illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.), shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective device.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall meet the general specifications of paragraph 4. and the specifications of shape and dimensions of Annex 5.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall withstand the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall withstand the water penetration test of Part 2 of Annex 6.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall withstand the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants of Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall, where necessary, withstand the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6.
The rear face of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall withstand the abrasive-strength test of Part 5 of Annex 6.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall meet the test for stability in time of the optical properties of Part 3 of Annex 4.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall withstand the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, after undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.

The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, after undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

Where more than one axis of reference or a range of axes of reference is specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements when measured with reference to each specified axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the specified range.

For photometric measurements of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector, the illuminating surface considered shall be that defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter.

The illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector considered for photometric measurements shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the illuminating surface area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.

The RI values of the red Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
For a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at illumination angles β1 = 0° and β2 = 0°, the RI value shall be not less than 3.00∙10^2 mcd·lx-1 at an angle of divergence α of 20'.
For a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at illumination angles β1 = 0° and β2 = 0°, the RI value shall be not less than 5 mcd·lx-1 at an angle of divergence α of 1°30'.
For a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at illumination angles β1 = ±10° and β2 = 0°, the RI value shall be not less than 2.00∙10^2 mcd·lx-1 at an angle of divergence α of 20'.
For a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at illumination angles β1 = ±10° and β2 = 0°, the RI value shall be not less than 2.8 mcd·lx-1 at an angle of divergence α of 1°30'.
For a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at illumination angles β1 = ±5° and β2 = ±20°, the RI value shall be not less than 1.00∙10^2 mcd·lx-1 at an angle of divergence α of 20'.
For a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at illumination angles β1 = ±5° and β2 = ±20°, the RI value shall be not less than 2.5 mcd·lx-1 at an angle of divergence α of 1°30'.

The RI values of the retro-reflector shall not be lower than those shown in the last two applicable columns of Table 3 within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

Where the Class IA or Class IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the red retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
Each Class IA or IB retro-reflector sample shall comply with the general specifications when subjected to visual inspection.
The retro-reflector shall be visually inspected for conformity of shapes and dimensions as specified in Annex 5.
The retro-reflector shall show no distortion on visual inspection after the heat test of 48 h at 65° ± 2°C as specified in Part 1 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2, verified by visual inspection and, in case of doubt, by trichromatic coordinates, after the heat test.
The retro-reflector shall meet the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, after the heat test.
The retro-reflector shall meet the complete photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4.
The retro-reflector shall show no water penetration on visual inspection after the water test of 10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position as specified in Part 3 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2 and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, after the water test.
The retro-reflector shall show no deterioration on visual inspection after exposure to motor fuels for 5 min as specified in Part 1 of Annex 7.
The retro-reflector shall show no deterioration on visual inspection after exposure to oils for 5 min as specified in Part 2 of Annex 7.
The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2 and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, after the motor fuel and oil tests.
The retro-reflector shall show no deterioration on visual inspection after the corrosion test of 24 hours, 2 hours interval and 24 hours as specified in Part 4 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall show no deterioration on visual inspection after the rear face test of 1 min as specified in Part 4 of Annex 6.

The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2 and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, after the corrosion and rear face tests.

The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2 and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, after the stability in time test of Part 3 of Annex 4.

The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2 and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, after the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates.

For a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP", the RI in the position of minimum RI, obtained by rotation about its axis of reference with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation) and an angle of divergence of 20', shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

For a retro-reflective device marked "TOP", the RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during rotation of ±5° about its axis, with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation) and an angle of divergence of 20'.

The moulded plastics retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall be subjected to a heat resistance test in which it is kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C and then allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device shall be visible.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the optical component of the retro-reflective device shall be visible.

The retro-reflector of the rear lamp, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface of the water.

The retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall withstand a repeated immersion for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C after being turned through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall withstand subsequent immediate immersion in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the rear lamp after the water immersion test.
The retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall be considered to have failed the water immersion test if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water.

Where visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall meet the RI requirements when measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of UN R150 after the water immersion test.
Where the moisture test is applied at the request of the manufacturer, the rear lamp shall resist moisture penetration from a water spray.
Where the moisture test is applied and the rear lamp has drain holes or other exposed openings, the rear lamp shall demonstrate drainage capability.
During the water spray moisture test, all drain holes and other openings of the rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector shall remain open.
Where drain wicks are used in the rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector, the drain wicks shall be tested in the device during the water spray moisture test.

Where the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test according to a cycle of 5 min ON and 55 min OFF.
The rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector shall be subjected to a water spray test lasting 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).

After completion of the water spray test and drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the retro-reflector device, nor shall one be able to be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
During the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the retro-reflector device shall remain open.
Where drain wicks are used, the drain wicks shall be tested in the retro-reflector device during the dust exposure test.

The retro-reflective device shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.

The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of its rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly where an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked, when tested for resistance to corrosion according to ISO Standard 9227:2017.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp where the device is combined with a light, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

Where the retro-reflective device has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, it shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6 at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.

After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6 at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not more than the value in Table 10.
The retro-reflective device shall withstand exposure in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.
The retro-reflective device shall be resistant to a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.

The outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular the illuminating surface, shall not show any apparent surface changes, except slight surface cracks, when inspected visually about five minutes after being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.

For a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall meet the RI requirements measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. after its outer surface, and in particular the illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes.
The approval number on the retro-reflective device shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number on the retro-reflective device shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.
Where the outer lens of the rear lamp is textured, the declared light emitting surface shall be all or part of the exterior surface of the outer lens.
Where the outer lens of the rear lamp is non-textured, the light emitting surface shall be as declared on the drawing, see Annex 3, and the outer lens may be disregarded.

The rear lamp shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
The rear lamp shall be fitted such that it is not possible for the lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The reference axis of each light-signalling device of the rear lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The reference axis of each light-signalling device of the rear lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The rear lamp shall be fitted in compliance with any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer.

In the absence of specific instructions, the rear lamp shall meet its height and orientation requirements with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.

In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, except with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the rear lamps shall satisfy the pair symmetry, colorimetric and photometric requirements so far as is possible.

Where the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, shall be fulfilled for each lamp.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp of the rear lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.

A single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed so that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except for a single retro-reflector.

A single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, shall be installed so that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro-reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or two independent retro-reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
A single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) (interdependent lamp system), shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included in the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, they shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Where the photometric characteristics of a lamp of the rear lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by the rear lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp of the rear lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front by the rear lamp shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of the white light emitted to the rear by the reversing lamp shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps if they exist, the side-marker lamps if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp.
The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall not be concealed.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light reflected by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflector shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

Where it is not practicable to prevent the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp or retro-reflector from being hidden more than 50 per cent by a movable component, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

Where more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp can be hidden by movable components and no additional lamps are provided, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements.
The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse, otherwise they are deemed not to be present.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is provided, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is provided, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.
During a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear lamp functions which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by special power supply provisions, the voltage at the terminals of the rear lamp device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by special power supply provisions, the voltage at the terminals of the rear lamp device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by special power supply provisions, the voltage at the terminals of the rear lamp device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the rear lamp observed from infinity, except obstacles already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the rear lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

Each lamp (device) of the rear lamp shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN Regulation No. 48 when installed on a vehicle.
Where a light-signalling lamp of the rear lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be present on motor vehicles.
One reversing lamp device shall be mandatory on motor vehicles of category M1, and a second reversing lamp device is optional.

The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.
The geometric visibility of the reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device.
The geometric visibility of the reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in a position where operation of the propulsion system is possible.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamps of S1 or S2 category shall be present on the vehicle.
The number of S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be two.
The stop lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of S1 or S2 category stop lamps which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be installed at a height above the ground of not less than 350 mm.

The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be installed at a height above the ground of not more than 1,500 mm, or not more than 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.
If optional S1 or S2 category stop lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

If optional S1 or S2 category stop lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a vertical distance above the mandatory lamps as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where an S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Where an optional S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the upward vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A stop lamp tell-tale indicating failure shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
The rear position lamp of R, R1 or R2 category shall be mandatory on the vehicle.
The number of rear position lamps shall be two.
The rear position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for optional rear position lamps.
For M1 category vehicles, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear position lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall have no special requirement.
The rear position lamp shall be mounted not less than 350 mm above the ground.

The rear position lamp shall be mounted not more than 1,500 mm above the ground, or not more than 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.

If optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements in width, the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
The rear position lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle may be reduced to 5°.
The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps shall be provided, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be provided if required by the component Regulation.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
The number of rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be two.

The rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with the position requirements) shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

The point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For M1 category vehicles, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, in the direction of the reference axes shall have no special requirement.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mounted not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mounted not more than 900 mm above the ground.
Where the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is grouped with any rear lamp(s), it shall be mounted not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
Where the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively, the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mounted not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall cover a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.
The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall cover a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal.

Where the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of geometric visibility may be reduced from 10° to 5°.
The orientation of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
A triangular rear retro-reflector shall not be fitted on motor vehicles, so the rear retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall not be triangular.

The rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, except that they may be switched OFF, and remain switched OFF, while the daytime running lamps are switched ON as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
An emergency stop signal shall be present on motor vehicles.
Where the emergency stop signal uses the stop lamps, it shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted, as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
Where the emergency stop signal is given by the stop lamps, the number of stop lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.2.
Where the emergency stop signal is given by the stop lamps, the arrangement of the stop lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.3.
Where the emergency stop signal is given by the stop lamps, the position of the stop lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.4.
Where the emergency stop signal is given by the stop lamps, the geometric visibility of the stop lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.5.
Where the emergency stop signal is given by the stop lamps, the orientation of the stop lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.7.6.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the hazard warning signal is activated.
Reversing lamps shall not be switched ON as exterior courtesy lamps.

Red light from the rear position lamp, stop lamp and rear retro-reflector shall not be visible to the eye of an observer moving within zone 1 in front of the vehicle. Zone 1 is bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground. It is bounded in width by a vertical plane forming an angle of 15° outwards to the front from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane and passing through the foremost point of contact of the vertical plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.

White light from the rear lamp, other than from the reversing lamp, shall not be visible to the eye of an observer moving within zone 2 behind the vehicle. Zone 2 is bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground. It is bounded in width by a vertical plane forming an angle of 15° outwards to the rear from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane and passing through the rearmost point of contact of the vertical plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.

The position in width, in height and in length of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector, measured in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of the Regulation, shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector, measured in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of the Regulation, shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The rear lamp shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.10. of the Regulation concerning visibility of red light towards the front.
The rear lamp shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.10. of the Regulation concerning visibility of white light towards the rear.

The rear position lamps, stop lamps and reversing lamps of the rear lamp, when switched on via the electrical system of the vehicle, shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48.
The rear position lamps, stop lamps and reversing lamps of the rear lamp shall function in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The tell-tales associated with the rear lamp functions shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the lamps and retro-reflectors of the rear lamp, as shown by the lamps and their markings, shall fulfil the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. of UN R48.
The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the lamps and retro-reflectors of the rear lamp shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
